stages.request: The registrar's office has a new import tool, and it rejects our term grades files because it expects fields separated by semicolons. Please make the term grades file that `gradebook export-grades` writes use `;` as its delimiter instead of `,`.

quiet.path: Following where the term grades file goes leads to `gradebook transcript`, whose `read_posted_grades` parses posted term grades files with a comma-separated reader.

stages.request: Teachers keep confusing the `points` scoring policy with the points a student scored on an assignment. Rename the policy to `total_points`. Course files that still say `"policy": "points"` must keep loading and grading exactly as before. When a course file names a policy that doesn't exist, loading it should now say `unknown scoring policy {name}; choose weighted or total_points`.

quiet.path: Searching for the policy name as a string finds the progress report's `_BASES` table, which looks up how to explain a grade by the course's policy name.

stages.request: Drop-lowest drops the wrong score when a category's assignments are worth different amounts. A student with 4/5 on one quiz and 6/10 on another has the 4/5 dropped, because 4 points is fewer than 6, even though 60% is the worse result. Course grades should rank scores for drop-lowest by percent of possible points, not by points earned.

quiet.path: Looking for everything that applies drop_lowest finds the progress report, which marks dropped scores and totals categories with its own ranking in `_lowest`.

stages.request: With one decimal place, too many students land right on a letter cutoff and we get grade disputes. Change the default of the course file option `grade_decimals` from `1` to `2`, so a course that doesn't set it rounds its percents to two decimals. Courses that set it keep their own value.

quiet.path: Reading every place a course grade percent is formatted shows the term grades export writes it with a fixed one decimal, relying on the old default rounding.

stages.request: Teachers fill in the score sheet from `gradebook sheet` by hand, and with only student ids on each row they keep typing scores on the wrong line. Add a `name` column right after `student_id`, with each student's name written as `Last, First`.

quiet.path: The score sheet module says sheets come back through `import sheet`; that importer treats every column except `student_id` as an assignment id.

stages.request: Add a `--sort` option to `gradebook report`. `--sort name` keeps today's order (last name, then first name) and stays the default; `--sort grade` lists the highest percent first, with students who have no grade yet at the end.

Add a `flat` late rule for course files: any late submission loses a fixed percent of the assignment's points, however many days late it is. The percent comes from the course file option `late.flat`, default `20`. Work handed in on time keeps every point, and a late penalty never takes a score below zero.

When a student has no graded work yet, their course grade has no letter, and the class report and the term grades file leave the letter blank, which looks like a data-entry mistake. Give them the letter `NG` (no grade) in all three places instead. Their percent stays empty.

quiet.path: Following the term grades file into transcripts shows `_credit_totals` treats a blank letter as no grade yet, the sentinel the new NG replaces.
